feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is iterations 0 to 3 (60 development trials each). Every run ended off track with exactly one line-loss event and max_error of about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Oscillation stayed low (0.08 to 0.15), so the robot is not weaving. Iteration 3 (base_speed 1.0, sensors at x = ±0.04, kp 2.5, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, line_loss last_direction, score 57.6) is the best raced design. Its oval progress rose to 0.21, but slalom and s-bend progress fell, so speed alone does not explain the failure. Gain changes (iteration 1) and the sensor span change (iteration 2) also left the failure point largely unchanged. The candidate keeps the iteration 3 geometry and gains and changes only controller.line_loss to search_right. That is the cleanest single-variable test of the recovery hypothesis (H4), and the telemetry cannot settle it without a race. The change is valid and not obviously broken, so it is worth racing now. Iterations remaining are limited, and a revise round would only repeat the same test. Read the next race this way. (1) If line_loss_events stays at 1 but progress rises clearly above 0.21 on the oval and above 0.13 on the s-bend, recovery mode was the limit, and the next step is to tune base_speed upward from 1.0 in small steps. (2) If max_error is clearly larger on the right edge, or progress falls, the robot is leaving on the wrong side. Test search_left next, which steers right. (3) If progress does not change at all, recovery mode is not the limit, and the next test is kp lowered from 2.5 toward 2.0 to reduce bend-entry turn authority.
requested_changes: Race the candidate as written, then compare progress, line_loss_events and max_error per track against iteration 3. If progress rises on the oval and s-bend, keep search_right and move base_speed up in small steps from 1.0.
If the failure side is clearly the right edge or progress drops, change only controller.line_loss to search_left and race again.
If progress is unchanged across tracks, keep the recovery mode and lower kp from 2.5 to 2.0 as the next single-variable test.
